approved_by: owner explicit GO in current conversation
hypothesis: Continuous SVG appearance may improve fixed coherent spline geometry without adding pixel cells.

conditions.A: strongest saved adaptive pixel winner for seven real cases; fixed watershed512 pixel control for two new analytic fixtures, not an adaptive search claim
conditions.B: saved inherited watershed128 cutout spline pilot08; same uniform config traced once for known-vector controls
conditions.C: identical B geometry, train-only optimized flat fills
conditions.D: identical C geometry; flat/linear/radial <=4 equally spaced stops selected using disjoint selection pixels

samples: periodic spatially disjoint train/selection/test; interpolation, not independent spatial/domain generalization
metrics: actual SVG SSIM PSNR MSE DeltaE76 highpass worst32px tile
alpha MAE max and premultiplied RGB
exact Bezier bounds cubic segments integer lattice shared segment pairs
native renderer and actual vector viewport crops1x4x16x
support_criterion: Held-out test and full-render gains beyond repeat noise on independent smooth cases at identical geometry; no new primitives. D>C is only appearance-capacity evidence, not milestone success.
rejection_criterion: No stable heldout/render gain, topology/geometry drift, illegal SVG/raster, or gains only from microgeometry. Any material gap to A remains failure to reach owner fidelity goal.
limitations: no promise of globally optimal fills
one uniform geometry granularity, not complete sweep
no physical/semantic ground truth on photographs
zeroalpha excluded; partial alpha weighted alpha²; actual composited full render remains decisive
